- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 90+), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 10% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- Forecast errors cluster near the end of 30-day horizon; true values often dip sharply in last 5–7 days; apply downward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate for suppressed momentum.
